content:
alex: Ran an nsys trace on the failing batch-run overnight. Timeline looks like memcpy H2D bursts then long gaps on stream 7 where kernels are queued but not executing. link: (internal nsys link)

sara: can you paste the command you used and the top-level timeline screenshot? curious about collection level and if cpu sampling was enabled

alex: command was: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,osrt -o /tmp/run1 ./bench --workload=kv-prefetch-test`\nattached small ascii waterfall:\n```
GPU stream 0: memcpy H2D [0-12ms]\nGPU stream 1: kernel A [12-14ms]\nGPU stream 7: memcpy H2D [15-18ms]\nGPU stream 7: kernel B queued [18-100ms] (idle)\nCPU: python main thread spikes at 17-18ms then sleeps until 100ms
```\n
maria: wow kernel B queued that long? suspicious. could be host spin waiting for a lock or a thread preempted between submitting kernels and some helper thread handling KV cache

dmitri: this matches an earlier hypothesis about the KV prefetch callback being executed on a background python worker that we don't pin. if that worker gets preempted by the OS, submission stalls. did you see any CPU scheduling gaps in the trace? (nsys has CPU lanes)

alex: yes nsys shows the host thread (tid 4312) running a small loop of `uv_poll` then a `pthread_cond_wait` but there are long gaps where it isn't scheduled. I also captured perfetto which shows linux sched_switch to another process at 17ms and back at 102ms. so ~85ms of preemption.

sara: 85ms is huge. what's the kernel runtime expected to be for kernel B? should be ~4ms on that config. so this delay is not GPU. check whether memcpy was issued from same stream or a different stream that has implicit ordering (cudaMemcpyAsync with default stream or stream per device?)

alex: memcpy and kernel B both use stream 7. memcpy completes, then we submit kernel B, but submission API returns quickly; however cudaLaunchKernel is synchronous w.r.t work submission to the driver and can still require CPU-side work. I instrumented NVTX around submit and saw the NVTX range start at 18ms but the corresponding driver CPU work didn't run until 102ms.

maria: NVTX helped. next step: try pinning prefetch thread to a dedicated CPU core and set SCHED_FIFO small rt prio to prevent preemption for test. also reduce cgroup CPU shares to reproduce more easily in CI.

dmitri: also try switching the KV prefetch callback to enqueue submission work to a dedicated submission thread that uses a lock-free queue. get rid of any Python-level GIL contention there. Even better: move submit into a small C++ helper bound to a core.

alex: I ran a quick experiment: pinned worker tid 4312 to cpu 10 and gave it SCHED_FIFO 50. Re-ran the trace. kernel B now starts at 19ms. no 80ms gap. So it's definitely host-side scheduling causing the latency.

sara: great repro. does this match the customer incident traces? if yes, we should add a mitigation in batching heuristics: if KV prefetch latency variance > X, fall back to smaller batch-size or prefer pre-warmed KV cache.

maria: agree. We should also: 1) add NVTX ranges for prefetch submission points across the codebase, 2) add a submission-thread mode toggle, 3) create a unit perf test that pulses CPU load to ensure we handle preemption gracefully.

dmitri: low-effort patch: wrap submit path with a spin-then-yield strategy. i can prototype a small change: attempt lockless submit, spin for up to 500us then yield. that might hide small preems without resorting to RT.

alex: note: we also saw hostmem cudaMemcpy being serialized on the copy engine in some traces when pinned threads exist, so ensure we don't overload the copy stream. Might need to use cudaMemcpyAsync into a pinned pool and stagger prefetches.

sara: action items:\n- dmitri: prototype spin-then-yield submit patch and run microbench (due EOD)\n- maria: add NVTX around prefetch submit + doc on submission-thread mode (due tomorrow)\n- alex: create CI perf test with induced CPU noise and attach traces (due in 2 days)\n- all: decide fallback policy for batching heuristics after the perf runs\n
perf-bot: perf regression check: nightly run shows 12.3% p50 increase for kv-prefetch workload on branch `feature/prefetch-rt` (compare base: main). See: (perf dashboard link)

maria: that aligns. the regression only appears when system CPU load is high, so I suspect the preemption path is the root cause rather than GPU changes.

alex: final note for the thread: we'll keep memcopy vs kernel overlap analysis in the follow-up doc. I captured a smaller 30s nsys with full CPU sampling and will paste links in the follow-up thread. thanks folks :thumbsup:
